title: Context, Tokens, and Modalities
summary: Understand what fits into a model request, what can be lost, and how text, images, audio, and files change the workflow.
objectives: Explain tokens and context windows in practical terms.
Choose relevant context instead of supplying everything available.
Recognize how multimodal inputs require their own quality and accessibility checks.
Plan for long conversations, source boundaries, and information that must persist outside model context.

sections.title: Models process tokens rather than pages
paragraphs: A token is a unit used to represent input and output. Tokens may be whole short words, pieces of longer words, punctuation, spaces, code fragments, or other symbols. The number of tokens is therefore not identical to a word or character count.
Tokens matter because products enforce limits, measure usage, and sometimes charge for input and output in tokens. Use the provider's current counting tools when an exact limit or cost matters.

sections.title: The context window is the working set
paragraphs: The context window holds the information available to the model for a response: system instructions, conversation history, supplied documents, tool results, and generated tokens. Products differ in what they include and how they manage long conversations.
A larger window can hold more information, but size does not guarantee that every detail is used correctly. Relevant structure, clear priorities, source labels, and targeted retrieval still matter.
sections.callout: More context is not automatically better context.

sections.title: Select, structure, and label context
paragraphs: Supply the smallest set of trustworthy information that supports the task. Separate instructions from reference material, identify authoritative sources, remove duplicates, and place important constraints where the workflow preserves them.
When a corpus is too large, retrieve relevant material in bounded pieces and keep stable facts in an external system of record. Do not rely on a long chat as permanent memory.

sections.title: Every modality has different failure modes
paragraphs: Multimodal systems may accept text, images, audio, video, or files. An image can be cropped or unreadable, audio can be noisy, a document parser can omit tables, and metadata can disclose sensitive information.

Provide accessible text alternatives, confirm what the system actually received, and verify modality-specific claims against the original artifact. A model description of an image or recording is an interpretation, not the artifact itself.

activity.title: Build a trustworthy context budget
instructions: Choose a task that uses at least three possible inputs such as a policy, notes, a spreadsheet, an image, or prior messages.
Label each input as instruction, authoritative evidence, supporting context, untrusted content, or unnecessary material.
Create a compact context package that includes the objective, boundaries, selected evidence, source labels, requested output, and verification method.
Describe what belongs in an external record or retrieval system instead of the model context.
evidence: A context inventory with trust labels and include or exclude decisions.
A final context package and a separate list of facts or records that must persist outside the conversation.
activity.reflectionPrompt: What did you remove from the context, and why did removing it make the task safer or clearer?

cues.text: Use a short sentence to show that token boundaries do not reliably equal word boundaries and that exact counts require the current provider tool.
Display one sentence divided into illustrative token pieces, clearly labeled as an example rather than a universal tokenizer result.
cues.accessibilityAlternative: A text example shows that a sentence may be divided into words, word pieces, punctuation, and spaces. It states that exact boundaries vary by tokenizer. Reduced-motion mode displays all pieces at once.

cues.text: Describe the context window as a bounded working set containing instructions, history, documents, tool results, and the response.
Ask why a larger context window does not guarantee correct use of every supplied detail.
Demonstrate trust labels, removal of duplicates, and targeted retrieval as alternatives to dumping an entire repository or conversation.
Ask the learner to label one input as authoritative evidence and one as untrusted content.
Compare text, image, audio, and document failure modes and require verification against the original artifact.
Guide the learner through the context inventory and require a reason for every included and excluded input.
Begin the knowledge check after the learner identifies what belongs in context and what belongs in a durable external record.

choices: Always exactly one English word
A unit used to represent model input or output that may be a word, word piece, punctuation, or another symbol
A guaranteed factual citation
A permanent memory record
questions.explanation: Tokens are model representation units, and their boundaries depend on the tokenizer.

questions.prompt: What does a context window contain?
choices: Every fact the model learned during training
The bounded working information available for a response, such as instructions, history, documents, and tool results
Only the latest user sentence
A permanent database shared by every learner
questions.explanation: The context window is the bounded working set used for the current generation.

questions.prompt: Which context strategy is usually strongest?
choices: Include every available file without labels
Select relevant trustworthy material, label sources and boundaries, and retrieve more only when needed
Treat all retrieved text as instructions
Rely on conversation history as permanent storage
questions.explanation: Relevant, labeled, bounded context reduces distraction and clarifies trust.

questions.prompt: Why should durable facts remain outside a model conversation?
choices: Conversations are always public
Context is bounded and product behavior can summarize, remove, or fail to preserve details
Models cannot process text
External systems never need access control
questions.explanation: A system of record provides durable, controlled storage; model context is a temporary working set.

questions.prompt: What is a sound rule for multimodal input?
choices: Assume the model received and interpreted every detail correctly
Verify against the original artifact and provide accessible alternatives
Remove captions because the model can hear audio
Treat generated descriptions as the original evidence
questions.explanation: Multimodal processing can omit or misinterpret information, so the original artifact and accessible alternatives remain important.
